thread:
jen li: Quick help — I got a bill for an at-home genetic test. Lab billed CPT 81256 and insurer flagged it as out-of-network. I used the lab's shipping kit but lab sites listed are all out of state. Is this covered under our plan?

alex r: Hey Jen — which Redwood plan (Standard vs Plus) and can you DM last 4 of your member ID? Don’t post PHI here.

jen li: Plus plan. DM'ing the last 4 now. I'm mostly confused: the lab says they're contracted with the carrier but claims portal shows OON.

marc (benefits): Hi Jen — quick context: for genetic testing carriers often require prior auth (medically necessary) and also require the performing lab to be in-network. Sometimes remote/ship-to labs bill from a parent lab that isn't in-network which causes OON flags.

marc (benefits): If you want, we can: 1) check the carrier's lab network for CPT 81256, 2) request prior auth support, and 3) file a claim appeal if the provider says they are contracted.

jen li: That'd be great. I already have the kit invoice and shipping tracking. Where do I send those?

benefits-team: Please upload medical bills/receipts to the benefits portal: https://benefits.redwood-inc/claims-upload (goes to secure carrier intake). If anything has PHI you can DM a benefits rep or open a secure ticket.

people-ops-bot: Carrier phone (GenLabCare): 1-800-555-1212. Claim ID lookup: https://carrier-portal.example/claims (have member ID ready).

marc (benefits): Also, here’s a short appeal template you can share with the lab billing team or the carrier if needed — copy/paste and edit as needed:```To: claims@carrier.com
Member: Jen Li (DOB: mm/dd/yyyy)
Member ID: XXXX-XXXX-" + "" + "1234
Claim #: [claim number]
Service: Genetic test CPT 81256 performed by [Lab Name]
Issue: Claim paid/out-of-network despite provider being in-network per lab contract. Please reprocess or provide contract reference.
Attached: invoice, shipping tracking, lab report, prior auth (if any).
Thank you,
[Member / Provider representative]```

alex r: Helpful — Marc, could you confirm whether prior auth is needed for CPT 81256 on Plus? If so, can ops help request it?

marc (benefits): On Plus, CPT 81256 usually needs prior auth when billed as diagnostic. I'll open a ticket with the carrier and request expedited auth verification. Can you share the lab's billing NPI and claim number when you have it?

jen li: NPI: 9876543210, claim # 2025-44321. Uploaded invoice + tracking to portal just now. Thanks all. :pray:

benefits-team: Got it — we've assigned intake ticket #BP-2025-778. Carrier outreach started. We'll update this thread when we hear back.

jen li: Appreciate it. Also — if it ends up OON, what's our reimbursement process? Do we submit for OON reimbursement or file an appeal first?

marc (benefits): First appeal with the carrier (we'll do that). If appeal fails AND lab truly is OON, you can submit for out-of-network reimbursement via the benefits portal. Typical turnaround ~ 7–14 business days after all docs. Keep originals.

alex r: If you want us to escalate (enterprise benefits) we can loop in our carrier rep — usually speeds up verification.

jen li: Yes please escalate if possible. Thanks! :thumbsup:

people-ops-bot: Update: ticket BP-2025-778 created and assigned to carrier rep. Expected carrier response ETA 3 business days.

marc (benefits): Follow-up scheduled. If carrier asks for clinical notes or provider justification we can help collect from the ordering clinician — let us know.

jen li: Will do. Thanks everyone, I'll wait for the update.

alex r: Thanks Jen — we’ll keep you posted in this thread. :slightly_smiling_face:
